newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium market balanced in 1997 - Billiton.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium market balanced in 1997 - Billiton.

text.p: The aluminium market looks to remain balanced this year, despite the sharp rebound in prices in recent months, brokers Billiton said on Monday in a weekly metals report.

"The market has certainly succeeded in establishing itself in a higher trading range, but in our view the fundamentals are not sufficiently inspiring to encourage further significant gains," the report said.
"We're looking for a pretty dull price environment during the current year."

Three-months prices have improved since plunging to 2-1/2 year lows last October, boosted by strength in copper, concerns over political instability in the former Soviet Union and talk of impending substantial London Metal Exchange (LME) stock drawdowns.

But although fund-based buying has helped push prices into a higher trading range, consumer interest has been disappointing and the market has struggled despite potentially supportive LME stock movements.
Any pent up demand, due in part to run-down consumer stocks, will encounter sufficient supplies, as last year's trend of increasing production is set to continue, the report said.
